I've been farming this land for 30 years. My mother taught me, her mother taught her. I know Quzhou's soil and weather the way I know my own hands. Some neighbors tried new things and lost money — I stick with what I know works here.

**My thinking:**

My 36 mu needs to earn money and feed the family. My husband does some work off-farm, so the farm is mostly on me and whoever's home. Cotton is the money crop — I sell it to the ginning station in autumn. Maize we keep some, sell some. Mungbean I grow a small plot because the price is decent and it doesn't take much work.

I'll put the most land in cotton — about 20 mu. It's hard work, all the spraying and picking, but I know how to do it. Maize gets 12 mu, mungbean gets 4 mu.

For cotton, I spray a lot — bollworm comes every year without fail. I won't skimp there. I'll plough the cotton field deep in spring like always. For maize, I'll use hybrid seed from the supply cooperative — everyone does now, it yields better. I'll rotary till that ground. Mungbean I keep simple — improved seed, not much fertilizer, it fixes some nitrogen anyway.

Water from the well — I know when the crops need it by looking at the leaves. Cotton I water more. Maize I water at silking if there's no rain.

I won't change much from last year. Last year was alright.
